cost.intro: Let's calculate what an outage costs. Two inputs:
cost.rev: Revenue that depends on the system, per hour (USD)
cost.result: A {h} h outage would cost you about {c} in revenue, not counting team hours or penalties. If you test the plan and cut the RTO in half, you save {s} per incident.Linear estimate. Source of the approach: DR Live project.

rpo.intro: Three questions to estimate your real RPO:
rpo.q1: How often does your latest valid backup or replica run?
rpo.q2: When did you last restore to test?
rpo.q3: Do you verify that backups complete successfully?
rpo.why: , because if a backup fails without you noticing, you lose the previous cycle's backup too
rpo.rtoNone: Your RTO today is unknown: without a test restore, it is only an estimate.
rpo.rtoOld: Your RTO is out of date: the environment has changed since the last test.
rpo.rtoOk: Your RTO has a recent measurement. Good.
rpo.calcCost: Calculate the cost of an outage
